17:23 Local Time, 21:23 GMT, 02:53 IST: The players are going off. Shamar Joseph came into the attack and the light-meter reading was checked. Salman offers a smile. He doesn't want to be batting in fading light for sure. But the day belonged to Pakistan. They were able to bowl out Windies for 311. It seemed it would be a bigger score but wasn't to be. Then Shan and Imam took charge after Azan was dismissed for a duck. Shan is unbeaten on 88. But Imam fell for a well made 64. Babar was looking good and solid till he edged one to the keeper. Shan would look to score his 100 and Salman would look to add much as he can. Day 3 is the moving day and we will surely see a big shift in the game tomorrow.

Imam-Ul-Haq: Look, when we were coming here, We knew it will swing. The Duke ball always swings. We knew it wasn't going to be easy. But we had a great last one month as a training group. As an opener, one needs to know his off-stump here. I was waiting for the ball to come in my range and then score runs. Simple plans coming here. My main focus to leave the ball well. Lucky it was my day. We thought we bowled well yesterday as well. We had the belief we will come back stronger. The bowlers - Mohammad Ali and Abbas - did a good job. Thanks to the Duke ball, the game changes quickly. The first session tomorrow will be very important for both sides. I really want to stick together and have a great partnership.

Alright then, Pakistan have edged ahead. Windies would need a couple of wickets early on day 3 to come right back in it. The wicket did seem to settle down towards the end of day 2. But a few balls have done enough for the bowlers to keep them interested. We will be back tomorrow. Hope you enjoyed our coverage today! Bye bye folks.

09:00 Local Time, 13:00 GMT, 18:30 IST: Shan Masood's sparkling 88* led Pakistan's reply after the hosts were bowled out for 311 in their first innings. The former Pakistan captain was involved in a 155-run second wicket stand with Imam-ul-Haq (63) as the pair revived the visitors after a shaky start. But the late dismissals of Imam and Babar Azam (23) have left the match still in balance. Will the balance shift in favour of Pakistan or the West Indies? Will Day 3 be the moving day of the Test? The ball is only 48 overs old and conditions are still ideal for batting. First ball of the day is coming up shortly..

Ravi Rampaul | West Indies bowling coach: I think we were inconsistent in our line and lengths. When we saw them bowl in the morning session, we thought there was a bit in the wicket, but as the sun baked, it became easier and we weren't consistent. We highlighted what went wrong (during the tea break), put the balls in similar places and waited for the results. Something happens when he bowls to right-handers (referencing Seales' dismissal of Babar Azam). He still has pain when he bowls (On Roston Chase), we'll continue to monitor and he'll be hopefully available later on in the day. Need to bowl in the right areas, we expect the ball to do a bit in the morning and we'll look for some early wickets.

It's bathed in sunshine - the cracks are increasing over a good length. A few of them have developed and there're footmarks of the fast bowlers. The left-arm spinner has a nice area which he can try to exploit. There's some movement still available, reckons Samuel Badree in his pitch report

13:21 local, 17:21 GMT, 22:51 IST: Justin Greaves walks off with the ball held aloft, acknowledging applause from all corners of the ground as he leads West Indies back to the pavilion. The all-rounder has every reason to soak in the moment after claiming his maiden Test five-for, the first by any bowler at this venue. Pakistan's innings ends at 282, but not before Khurram Shahzad and Mohammad Ali add some valuable runs for the final wicket to frustrate West Indies after lunch. The damage, however, had already been done in the opening session. After Masood's superb hundred, Shamar Joseph's wicket of Salman Agha sparked a collapse, with Greaves ripping through the lower order in a remarkable spell of five successive wicket maidens - four before lunch and one immediately after the break. The hosts now hold a 29-run lead and will look to press home their advantage for the rest of the day. Back shortly...
